replaces: the shell CHAIN agent monitor path for runner-v2 launches. The legacy helpers remain only as historical/reference surfaces outside the typed launch path; lib/mentiko-monitor.sh is the separate manual CLI and not a chain-launch fallback.
preserves: docs/orchestration/contracts/monitor.contract.json is the v1 behavior of record; every invariant and behavior there must survive the port unchanged unless explicitly superseded below

why.problem: the monitor — the loop that watches an agent over time and owns the patient 'wait, nudge, then latch' behavior — is still shell, while the completion verdict (a one-shot) is typed. The shell monitor is PATIENT: it nudges a stalled-but-alive agent and only latches completion on a real declared event or a standalone AGENT_COMPLETE. But the typed completion bridge it invokes runs its OWN blind retry/exhaust with no view of liveness. That split-brain — patient shell watcher, impatient typed verdict — is exactly what failed TASK-093: the typed bridge exhausted and declared the agent failed while the agent was still alive and emitted its declared event ~4.5 minutes later.
why.fix: unify the watch loop and completion verdict under one typed owner and one completion-evidence probe. Completion is invoked only for a declared event, a standalone AGENT_COMPLETE in the current-attempt durable transcript, or a compatible canonical generation-result.json owned by a core generation run. Every terminal path rechecks that evidence before mutation; an alive evidence-free agent is never speculatively completed.
why.deletion_gate: Legacy monitor files may remain for unrelated/manual entrypoints, but runner-v2 launch and routing must invoke only the compiled typed monitor. A typed monitor failure fails closed rather than re-entering a shell monitor.

spawn.current: web/lib/runner-v2/agent-bootstrap-plan.ts buildMonitorCommand and lib/chain-runner.sh routed scripts execute compiled lib/monitor-v2.js with the exact session argv and explicit run context.
spawn.v2: Compiled monitor-v2 is the sole runner-v2 monitor command; PTY spawn, env carry, and singleton semantics remain explicit.
spawn.fallback: none. Missing bundle, invalid context, unsupported input, or a non-zero typed monitor exit fails closed.

entrypoints.env_carry: the monitor command preserves the explicit run context. On completion, completion-launch.ts copies the allowlisted values into a private one-shot 0600 file because the PTY daemon filters spawn env; only the random path enters completion PTY argv, and validated deletion is the child-acceptance receipt.

monitor_loop.watch: poll the session capture on an interval (shell: lib/mentiko-monitor.sh while-loop with CHECK_INTERVAL); the typed port keeps the same poll-until-terminal shape and must NOT block or run inside the completion PTY
monitor_loop.completion_latch: OR-latch from authoritative evidence: a standalone AGENT_COMPLETE line in the current-attempt durable transcript, a declared emits event owned by this agent/run, or a compatible canonical generation-result.json whose core-chain/run/job/token/attempt freshness boundaries agree. Latch recorded at ~/.mentiko_monitor/${session}_complete.
monitor_loop.stale: md5 of the last 20 captured lines unchanged marks a stale tick (advisor_threshold MENTIKO_ADVISOR_STALE_COUNT default 3, max_stale default 5). Stale drives advisor nudges / blocked diagnostics ONLY — never completion. 'stale output does not imply completion.'
monitor_loop.nudge_budget: durable ceiling MENTIKO_MONITOR_MAX_NUDGES tracked in ~/.mentiko_monitor/${session}_nudges; survives screen-echo stale resets and monitor restarts; an exhausted budget escalates (awaits latch) instead of nudging forever (20ce3b1). The typed port MUST persist this to disk, not memory, or a monitor restart resets the budget.
monitor_loop.death: local workspaces: pgrep the child process under the pane pid. remote (ssh/docker): SKIP local process-death checks. Death classification is EVENT-FIRST: process gone WITH a genuine completion event -> complete normally; process gone WITHOUT an event -> failed diagnostic agent-error (agent-functions.sh monitor-agent-died).
monitor_loop.liveness_wins: an agent whose session is alive and still producing output is NEVER classified dead or failed for a missing event; the loop keeps watching and nudging within budget. This is the structural form of runner-v2-contract.json completion_liveness_contract.liveness_wins — enforced here by the component that actually observes liveness.

completion_handoff.invoke: the monitor launches the completion verdict in a separate pty and only on authoritative event/marker/core-generation-artifact evidence; a validated generation artifact is the explicit exception to the eventless rule because generation-result.json is the product handoff
completion_handoff.shared_liveness: because the typed monitor already holds the liveness view, it either (a) passes that view into the typed completion verdict, or (b) simply does not invoke completion until the agent is genuinely done. Either way the typed completion's blind retry/exhaust — the root of TASK-093 — is removed. This is where completion-runner.ts evaluateAgentLiveness/await-liveness finally receives a real signal from its true owner.
completion_handoff.one_owner: exactly one owner applies completion side effects. In the typed path there is NO shell completion fallback; the typed monitor + typed completion are the single owner. A typed exit 64 or completion PTY spawn failure fails closed instead of execing/nohuping shell completion.
completion_handoff.no_blind_exhaustion: the migrated path MUST NOT contain a completion verdict that terminalizes an agent for a missing event without the monitor's liveness view. Blind exhaustion is the specific defect being removed; a parity test must prove a stalled-but-alive agent is never failed.

death_latch_ordering.rule: authoritative completion evidence is evaluated before process death, session disappearance, stall escalation, and context exhaustion. A handoff that became durable before terminal mutation always wins.
death_latch_ordering.reducer_order: monitor-reducer remains session-gone -> latched -> processGone -> hash, while monitor.ts performs the authoritative evidence probe before handling session-gone or any other non-success terminal action.
death_latch_ordering.onDied_race_guard: the driver probes once after classification and the live terminal callback probes the same evidence source again immediately before mutation; late valid events retain the reconciler backstop and generation artifacts retain explicit typed completion re-entry.

command_contract.typed_argv: monitor-v2 <session> <interval> <context> <chainPath> <maxStale> — argv is the sole runner-v2 monitor command for both initial and routed launches
env: MENTIKO_CODE_ROOT (engine-anchored; the completion session cwd lives in the data root)
command_contract.exit_codes: 0 = the monitor ran to a terminal verdict (complete / died / stalled / session-gone) and handled it; every non-zero exit is a typed operational failure that fails closed. The monitor owns its loop.
command_contract.selection: Runner-v2 launch and routing always invoke compiled monitor-v2; there is no monitor selection flag or shell compatibility branch.

readiness_gate.blocks_until: readiness MUST NOT pass on a typed monitor that does not also fix the TASK-093 failure mode. Proven before default switch: (1) the monitor invokes completion ONLY on a genuine latch, never while the agent is alive and eventless (monitor-reducer proves it: alive+producing -> active, never complete); (2) death is event-first (classifyDeath) and latch wins over death; (3) live TASK-093-shaped proof completes through monitor-v2 and typed completion with terminalReason completed_from_event; (4) late-event recovery is connected through the task reconciler for already-stuck legacy false failures.
readiness_gate.no_half_fix: a typed monitor loop WITHOUT the completion handoff wired was explicitly NOT done. That handoff is now proven, and recoverLateCompletionEvents is connected before terminal retry/audit handling; default readiness can pass when the contract-binding gate is otherwise clean.

readiness_binding.requirement: the monitor-v2 invariants MUST be enforced by the switch-readiness contract-binding gate (web/lib/runner-v2/switch-readiness.ts + switch-readiness.binding.test.ts) — the same gate that refuses any unbound owns/invariants line. This is wired through docs/orchestration/contracts/monitor-v2.contract.json in IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_FILES.
readiness_binding.how: bind every line in runner-v2-contract.json implementation_coverage['monitor-v2.contract.json'] with status covered (evidence: monitor-reducer.ts / monitor.ts / monitor-diagnostics.ts / monitor-live-io.ts + their tests/proofs) or an explicit gap/shell-owned. The existing switch-readiness.binding.test.ts fails on any unbound monitor-v2 line automatically.
readiness_binding.test: a test MUST fail if any monitor-v2 invariant is unbound; once monitor-v2.contract.json is in IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_FILES, switch-readiness.binding.test.ts provides exactly this.

superseded_or_not_applicable.exported-fn heredoc / export -f serializ: NOT APPLICABLE — a shell-source hygiene invariant with no TypeScript analogue; the typed monitor is a node module, not an export -f'd bash function.
superseded_or_not_applicable.md5-of-last-20-lines stale detector: PRESERVED as the default, but the port MAY substitute a proven-equivalent change detector that never weakens 'stale is not complete' (the shell itself notes md5 is known-blind to spinner redraws).

disk_contracts.capture_source: the pty session capture (transport capture) the shell monitor md5s; AGENT_COMPLETE is resolved against the DURABLE session transcript JSONL (by session UUID), never the re-wrappable rendered screen (BUG-022 durable-evidence latch), so a resized instruction echo cannot false-latch

parity_requirements: md5-of-last-20-lines stale detection reproduced, or a proven-equivalent change detector that never regresses 'stale is not complete'
durable nudge budget persisted to disk, surviving screen-echo stale resets and monitor restarts
AGENT_COMPLETE latch requires a standalone marker in the uniquely identified current-attempt DURABLE transcript JSONL, never the rendered screen (BUG-022)
transcript resolution uses the selected profile log_path and fails closed on missing or ambiguous current-attempt identity
core generation artifact evidence uses the shared generation payload validator and canonical run-scoped artifact path
event match respects agent id (source superstring) and run id
death classification is event-first, and skips local process-death checks for ssh/docker workspaces
completion handler runs in a separate pty, never the monitor pty
singleton/daemon spawn semantics and full env carry preserved
invariants: dead without declared event is not success
completion matcher never accepts monitor diagnostic events
AGENT_COMPLETE must be a standalone durable-transcript line (BUG-022)
event match respects agent id and run id
completion handler runs outside the monitor pty
screen-echo repaints never grant more nudges: the nudge budget is durable (20ce3b1)
liveness wins: never classify an alive, producing agent as dead or failed for a missing event
death is event-first: process gone WITH a completion event completes normally
the monitor is the re-check loop: completion is invoked only on authoritative evidence, so no verdict makes a blind, liveness-unaware exhaustion decision (the TASK-093 fix)
actionable blocked runs retain their owned agent PTY; handled terminal outcomes verify namespaced monitor-then-agent cleanup and persist retryable failures
runner-v2 monitor failures fail closed and never re-enter shell monitoring
known_gaps: automatic periodic reconciliation of a core generation artifact that lands after both terminal probes remains separate from the explicit typed completion recovery path; the monitor closes both in-loop race windows before terminal mutation

the shell md5-of-20-lines detector is heuristic and known-blind to spinner redraws (agent-functions.sh comment); the port should preserve behavior but may improve the change detector without weakening 'stale is not complete'
remote (ssh/docker) liveness has no local pid to pgrep; the typed monitor must reproduce the shell remote-skip and lean on event/transcript evidence for those workspaces
the monitor is a long-lived per-agent PTY loop, not a one-shot; the typed port must handle its own restart/idempotency (durable latch + nudge files) the way the shell monitor does
migration_plan: 2. typed monitor loop: watch + latch + stale + durable nudge + event-first death, at parity with the historical behavior, with typed completion handoff proven live
3. wire buildMonitorCommand and routed launch scripts to execute compiled monitor-v2 with full env carry and no shell fallback
4. unify the completion handoff: the typed monitor invokes the typed completion verdict with a shared liveness view (or gates invocation on genuine-done); remove the blind exhaustion path
5. parity tests cover every invariant; a runtime proof on a real stalled-but-alive agent (the TASK-093 shape) shows the agent is nudged/awaited and never falsely failed
6. retain legacy monitor files only for explicitly separate/manual behavior; runner-v2 launch must never select them
